source_text:
Ἐγράψαμεν ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὰ κατὰ τοὺς μαρτυρήσαντας καὶ τὸν μακάριον Πολύκαρπον, ὅστις ὥσπερ ἐπισφραγίσας διὰ τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτοῦ κατέπαυσεν τὸν διωγμόν. σχεδὸν γὰρ πάντα τὰ προάγοντα ἐγένετο, ἵνα ἡμῖν ὁ κύριος ἄνωθεν ἐπιδείξῃ τὸ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον μαρτύριον.
περιέμενεν γάρ, ἵνα παραδοθῇ, ὡς καὶ ὁ κύριος, ἵνα μιμηταὶ καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοῦ γενώμεθα, μὴ μόνον σκοποῦντες τὸ καθ̓ ἑαυτούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ κατὰ τοὺς πέλας. ἀγάπης γὰρ ἀληθοῦς καὶ βεβαίας ἐστίν, μὴ μόνον ἑαυτὸν θέλειν σώζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀδελφούς.
thought_title: The martyrdom of Polycarp as a seal upon the persecution
orientation: The church of Smyrna, writing to the church in Philomelium, begins its account by explaining why Polycarp's martyrdom matters: it followed the pattern of the Lord's own passion and crowned the recent martyrdoms.
pass_a_gloss: We wrote to you, brothers, the things concerning those who bore martyrdom and the blessed Polycarp, who, as if having set a seal through his martyrdom, brought the persecution to an end. For nearly all the things that went before happened, in order that the Lord might show to us from above the martyrdom according to the gospel. For he waited, in order that he might be handed over, just as also the Lord, in order that we also might become imitators of him, not only looking at what concerns ourselves, but also at what concerns our neighbors. For it is of true and firm love, not only to wish oneself to be saved, but also all the brothers.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'martyr' for μάρτυς; the participle here denotes those who underwent martyrdom, so 'bore martyrdom' preserves the verbal force and the glossary term.
The metaphor is of sealing or confirming the persecution's end; 'set a seal upon' keeps the concrete image of a seal as a confirming mark.

choices.english: brought the persecution to an end
choices.why: The verb καταπαύω means to cause to cease; 'brought to an end' is literal and clear.
rejected: put a stop to the persecution

choices.english: the martyrdom according to the gospel
choices.why: The glossary requires 'martyrdom' for μαρτύριον; 'according to the gospel' renders κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον literally.
rejected: the martyrdom in line with the gospel

choices.why: ἀληθοῦς means true, βεβαίας means firm or steadfast; both adjectives are rendered plainly.

pass_b_english: We have written to you, brothers and sisters, about those who bore martyrdom and about the blessed Polycarp, who by his martyrdom set a seal upon the persecution and brought it to an end. For nearly everything that went before happened so that the Lord might show us from above the martyrdom according to the gospel.

For he waited to be handed over, just as the Lord did, so that we too might become his imitators, not looking only to our own concerns, but also to the concerns of our neighbors. For it is the mark of true and firm love to desire not only one's own salvation, but also the salvation of all the brothers and sisters.

last_rejected.why: σχεδὸν modifies 'all', meaning 'almost all', not 'nearly everything' as extent of time.
last_rejected.fix: For almost all the things that preceded happened
last_rejected.ruling: σχεδὸν πάντα = 'nearly all things'; 'nearly everything' is equivalent. No meaning change.

last_rejected.why: τὰ προάγοντα means 'the things that preceded/led up to this', not 'went before' in time vaguely.
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ προάγοντα = 'things going before/preceding'; 'went before' captures this adequately.

last_rejected.why: Subject is Polycarp (masculine), but 'he' is ambiguous; could refer to Lord. Greek has no article with περιέμενεν, but context shows Polycarp waited.
last_rejected.ruling: 'he' naturally refers to Polycarp, the subject; ambiguity is minor, not misleading.

last_rejected.why: τὸ καθ᾽ ἑαυτούς / τὸ κατὰ τοὺς πέλας means 'what concerns oneself/one's neighbors', not 'concerns' as worries.
last_rejected.ruling: 'concerns' = 'what concerns X'; standard rendering of τὸ κατὰ + acc. No meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified that Polycarp is the one who waited to be handed over, removed the em dash, and kept the sentence flow natural for reading aloud while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.quote: the martyrdom according to the gospel
notes.why: Technical phrase never defined; implies specific ideal pattern.
notes.fix: Add note: 'martyrdom patterned on Christ's passion.'
